personality_one_liner: A calm, typography-first sanctuary for reading, using generous whitespace and classic serif fonts to elevate the scripture.

spacing.rule: Generous vertical breathing room. Treat the interface like a printed book. No cramped cards or tight lists.

dont's: No glassmorphism. This is an Editorial app; rely on flat colors, stark contrast, and matte paper-like textures.

screens.name: Home
screens.purpose: A serene dashboard highlighting the Verse of the Day, reading progress, and quick access to continue reading.

states.error: Failed to load cached Verse of the Day, showing an offline fallback verse.

screens.layout: Top half is a hero card (Verse of the Day) with a full-bleed calm background image, layered with a vertical gradient scrim, and elegant Lora typography. Below the hero: 'Continue Reading' card spanning full width, and a 2-column grid for 'Progress' and 'Streak' metrics.

screens.name: Read (Library & Reader)
screens.purpose: The core scripture reading experience, allowing navigation from Book -> Chapter -> Verse.
screens.layout: Library: A clean list of books, heavily reliant on whitespace and subtle dividers. Chapter Grid: Simple numeric tiles. Reader View: Edge-to-edge text using Lora font, justified or left-aligned depending on size, generous line height (1.6+). Header hides on scroll. A floating 'Settings/Translation' pill at the bottom.

screens.name: Search

states.empty: Illustration of an open book with prompt to search keywords.

screens.layout: Prominent search input (flat, borderStrong bottom border only, no rounded box) at the top. Results are presented as a flat list with the Book/Chapter/Verse in DMSans (UI font) and the verse excerpt in Lora (Serif).

screens.name: Bookmarks
screens.purpose: List of saved verses and highlighted passages.

states.empty: Illustration of a bookmark and 'No verses saved yet.' message.

screens.layout: Standard single-column editorial list. Each item shows the verse text prominently in Lora, with metadata (Book Chapter:Verse) in smaller DMSans above it. Swipe to delete.

screens.name: Progress
screens.purpose: Visual representation of reading completion and streaks.
screens.layout: Editorial presentation of data. Large typography for percentages and streak days instead of generic progress bars. Use whitespace and typography to group 'Chapters Visited' and 'Daily Streak'.

instructions_to_main_agent: ADHERE STRICTLY TO THE EDITORIAL LIGHT PERSONALITY: Rely entirely on flat surfaces, generous whitespace (xl/2xl), and elegant typography. Do not introduce shadows or glassmorphism.

BANNED COLORS: Strictly avoid any blues, indigos, purples, or typical 'tech' palettes. Use the provided warm cream/off-white (light mode) and soft dark-gray (dark mode) as surfaces, and muted rust/terracotta for brand accents.

TYPOGRAPHY HIERARCHY: Use Lora (Display/Serif) exclusively for scripture, verse text, and major headings. Use DMSans (Text/Sans) for UI elements, tabs, metadata, settings, and buttons. Do not exceed font-weight 500.

VERSE HIGHLIGHTING UX: When a user taps or long-presses a verse, avoid default system selection handles if possible (as they are clunky). Instead, wrap verses in Pressables and trigger a custom BottomSheet (via @gorhom/bottom-sheet) to select highlight colors (Yellow, Red, Green) or Copy to Clipboard.

IMAGE SCRIM MANDATE: For the Verse of the Day card on the Home screen, layer a 3-stop vertical gradient scrim (transparent -> 20% surfaceInverse -> 70% surfaceInverse) between the image and the text to ensure the Lora text is perfectly legible.

LOCAL STORAGE ARCHITECTURE: All states (bookmarks, highlights, progress, dark mode preference) must be strictly persisted using AsyncStorage or a local SQLite/WatermelonDB equivalent if the text bundle is large. Do not set up a remote backend.
OFFLINE TRANSLATIONS: Ensure the UI provides a seamless, instant toggle between the offline bundled KJV and WEB texts, preferably via a subtle floating action pill or a top right header icon.
